And therefore our Sages taught [Bamidbar Rabbah, Mishpatim]: "all who take interest — Scripture accounts it as if one did all the evils and transgressions in the world" — etc. — "and the Holy One says: until now he was alive." As stated — for one thereby damages the overall rectifications of holy Torah — through which one merits the holy life-force. And one who lends without interest — it is as if one did all the commandments — for this is the aspect of the general totality of all the commandments of holy Torah — to draw through them the aspects of these rectifications. And therefore our Sages taught: charity equals the entire Torah and the commandments — and loving-kindness is greater than charity — see further there in the Midrash mentioned and you will understand for our subject.

[§6] And this: the mitzvah to taste from the Shabbos dishes on Erev Shabbos — for our Sages taught that Yaakov took as his portion the World to Come — and yet he is also of necessity obligated to pass through this world — only that in truth the aspect of Yaakov has no desire or will for any worldly matter — rather even his this-worldly affairs are only for the World to Come — and all his actions are only for Heaven's sake.

aligned_segments.he: כי העיקר הוא אתערותא דלתתא של זה העולם כידוע וע"כ בזה מעוררין אותו ומוסיפין לו כח ביותר לעשות חיל ולילך גם שם בכך פעם ממדריגה למדריגה גבוה ביותר בבחי' ילכו מחיל אל חיל וכמ ושדרז,ל על זה באמת כי לגדולתו י"ת אין חקר ולתבונתו אין מספר:
aligned_segments.en:
It follows that in his this-world as well he tastes the flavor of the World to Come — and this is alluded to in the tasting of the Shabbos dishes on Erev Shabbos.

סִימָן קס״ז — הִלְכוֹת בְּצִיעַת הַפַּת

 
 [§1]
 And this is the aspect of the blessing HaMotzi [Who brings forth] — 
 for one blesses Hashem, Who has placed such power and life-force inwardly 
 within the earth — which alludes to the aspect of Malchus — 
 the last of the four elements and the densest and most coarse of them all — 
 for it alludes to the ultimate in contractions — 
 such that, to all appearances judging by human eyes and intellect, 
 it seems utterly remote from the aspect of holy life-force and wisdom. And yet there is concealed within it a spiritual power of such a nature 
 that even bread — upon which all of human life depends — 
 also grows from the earth. And from this it is understood and seen: 
 that the Creator brought all of Creation into being in such a way 
 that in every thing in the world — even at the ultimate extreme of physical coarseness — 
 there is concealed within it holy wisdom and intellect of such a nature 
 that if a person sets his eyes and heart upon this, 
 he can thereby draw close to Hashem and cleave to Him — 
 and this is the essence of true life in its fullness.
 

 
 [§2]
 And therefore one must break [the bread] at the place where it is most baked — 
 where the fire has acted most strongly — 
 for the essential rectification of flour — which alludes to Malchus — as is known — 
 is through fire — which is the aspect of the Torah, which is compared to fire — 
 in the aspect of what our Sages taught: 
 "if it is stone, it will be dissolved; if it is iron, it will be shattered" — 
 as it is said: *"Is not My word like fire?"* [Yirmiyahu 23:29] — etc. And this is the aspect of: "if there is no Torah, there is no flour" [Avos 3:17] — 
 for the power of holy Malchus to overpower the sitra achra 
 is through the holy Torah — 
 and through this Malchus ascends and receives from the aspect of holy Chochmah — 
 which is also the aspect of fire among the four elements — as is known. And therefore at the place where the fire has acted most strongly in the bread — 
 there one must break and bless.
 

 
 [§3]
 One should prefer to bless over a whole loaf — 
 for holy Chochmah is the essential wholeness — 
 as our Sages taught: "If you have acquired wisdom, what do you lack?" — 
 and as is explained in the discourse Atika, Siman 21 — 
 and likewise the entire holy Torah is described: 
 *"the Torah of Hashem is perfect"* [Tehillim 19:8].
 

 
 [§4]
 And therefore one must hold the bread with both hands — 
 with ten fingers — 
 corresponding to the ten mitzvos associated with bread — 
 to teach that the essential rectification of the bread 
 is through the mitzvos of the holy Torah — 
 and through this one can merit to receive through the eating of bread 
 holy vitality from the aspect of Chochmah — 
 which is the aspect of Yud — as is known.
 

 
 [§5]
 And as the Shulchan Aruch states: 
 corresponding to this, there are ten words in the blessing HaMotzi — 
 ten words in the verse *"He causes grass to grow for the cattle"* [Tehillim 104:14] — 
 meaning: in this verse it is alluded that in order to merit the aspect of Chochmah — 
 which is the essential life and definition of the human being — 
 it is impossible [to achieve this] except through the aspect of Malchus — 
 alluded to in the word behemah [cattle] — as is known. And therefore the verse begins: "He causes grass to grow for the cattle" — 
 and then: "to bring forth bread from the earth." 
 And therefore it is forbidden to eat before feeding one's cattle first — as stated above. And there are also ten words in the verse 
 *"the eyes of all look to You with hope"* [Tehillim 145:15] — 
 for one must know that all livelihood flows only through trust [in G-d] — 
 and one merits trust only through wisdom and intellect — as explained in Siman 225. And there are ten words in the verse 
 *"a land of wheat and barley"* [Devarim 8:8] — 
 for the Land of Israel is the aspect of Malchus — as is known — 
 and receives its abundance from the supernal Chochmah — 
 in the aspect of: the air of the Land of Israel makes one wise. And therefore it contains ten levels of sanctity — 
 corresponding to Chochmah — the aspect of Yud — the aspect of Kodesh. And there are also ten words in the verse 
 *"and He will give you"* — [Bereishis 27:28] — 
 for all influences and all blessings flow in their root 
 from the aspect of Chochmah — which is the source of blessing.
 

 
 [§6]
 One must place salt on the table — 
 for salt also alludes to the person's intellect and wisdom — 
 for according to nature, everything depends on the abundance of saline content 
 in one's constitution — as the scholars of alchemy clarified. And the commentators explained through this the intent of our Sages' words 
 [Kiddushin 29b]: "if a son is sharp and well-seasoned" — etc. And therefore in the Temple it is said: 
 *"upon all your offerings you shall offer salt"* [Vayikra 2:13] — 
 for sacrifices are primarily intended to break the animal spirit and foolishness within oneself — 
 which is from the side of the yetzer hara — 
 in the aspect of *"the sacrifices of G-d are a broken spirit"* [Tehillim 51:19] — 
 and to merit holy Chochmah — 
 therefore salt is prescribed with them.
 

 
 [§7]
 The table atones like the altar — 
 for the time of eating is a time of battle — as is explained in the holy Zohar. In its plain sense, one must at that time battle with one's desires — 
 which are only from the side of the yetzer hara — 
 and fulfil what our Sages said: 
 "at a meal that gives you pleasure, withdraw your hand from it." 
 And in its inner dimension, the eating itself is a form of battle — 
 for one draws out at that time very holy sparks 
 that were until then clothed within such physical grossness and waste — 
 and all of this is only through the power of bonding to holy Chochmah — 
 for "all of them are clarified through thought" [Zohar] — 
 and therefore it too atones like the altar — and requires salt. And therefore one must speak words of Torah at the table — 
 for the entire power of holy Malchus to overpower the sitra achra 
 and extract what it has swallowed — 
 all of this is only through the power of Torah study — as stated.
 

 
 [§8]
 Lechem u'Melach [bread and salt] in numerical value equals Yosef — 
 for Yosef merited both aspects most fully — 
 and therefore he merited chen [grace] — as is explained within.

aligned_segments.he: וזה בחי' מצוות הלויית המת.
aligned_segments.en:
And therefore it is said of him explicitly: 
 *"and Yosef — he was the ruler"* [Bereishis 42:6] — the aspect of Malchus — 
 and it is said of him: 
 *"there is none as discerning and wise as you"* [Bereishis 41:39] — 
 the aspect of Chochmah.
 

 
 [§9]
 And therefore one is particular to bless over the whole loaf — 
 which alludes to Chochmah — as stated — 
 and also over the larger [loaf] and the more beautiful — 
 which alludes to Malchus and greatness — 
 as it is said: *"a king in his beauty your eyes shall behold"* [Yeshayahu 33:17]. And likewise regarding wisdom: *"a person's wisdom illuminates his face"* [Koheles 8:1]. And the essential ascent of a person from the aspect of smallness 
 to the aspect of greatness [gadlus] is 
 only in the matter of the mochin and Chochmah — 
 the aspect of mochin d'gadlus — the aspect of gadol da'as [great in knowledge]. And likewise the essential perfection of Malchus is when it is 
 complete — in the aspect of what our Sages taught: 
 "one who wishes to accept upon himself the complete yoke of Heavenly Kingship" — 
 and its essential completeness is when it is joined with its Beloved 
 and receives from the light of holy Chochmah — as stated — 
 and then it is called sheleimah [complete] — for it completes all things — as is known.

סִימָן ק״ע–קע״א — דְּבָרִים הַנּוֹהֲגִים בַּסְּעוּדָה

 
 [§1]
 One does not speak during the meal — even words of Torah — 
 lest the windpipe precede the gullet — 
 for in the matter of the meal, the entire affair explained regarding Yaakov and Esav is found — 
 as the verse says: 
 *"the first one came out red"* [Bereishis 25:25] — etc. — 
 and: *"and afterwards his brother came out, with his hand grasping the heel of Esav"* — etc. — 
 and Yaakov gave Esav bread and a pottage of lentils — 
 *"and he ate and drank and rose and went, and Esav despised the birthright"* — 
 and its Targum [Onkelos]: "and Esav cast off the birthright." 
 And it is cited that Esav's hold is in the aspect of the veshet [gullet] — 
 in the aspect of "and Esav cast off" — 
 the aspect of this world, which involves eating and drinking — all through the gullet. And Yaakov is in the aspect of the kaneh [windpipe] — 
 in the aspect of "acquire wisdom" [Mishlei 4:5] — 
 the aspect of the World to Come, which has no eating or drinking.
 

 
 [§2]
 During eating, the food passes through the gullet — the aspect of Esav — 
 and the liver is nourished first — which is also the aspect of the red Esav — 
 and afterwards it sends [nourishment] to the heart and the brain — 
 which are the aspect of Yaakov. And when one eats with proper intention — 
 in the aspect of *"the righteous eats to satisfy his soul"* [Mishlei 13:25] — 
 minimizing bodily desire — 
 then he is in the aspect of "the elder shall serve the younger" — 
 for even though the body is nourished first, 
 everything is only for the sake of the soul and holy life-force — which is Chochmah. And this itself is the aspect of the salt — 
 for during the meal, even though the act of eating and drinking is from the side of Esav, 
 one should nevertheless endeavor to be in the aspect of 
 "and his hand grasps the heel of Esav" — 
 to break one's desire — 
 and in one's thought to direct even one's eating solely for the sake of Heaven — 
 for the sake of life and sustenance in the service of one's Creator.
 

 
 [§3]
 And it is precisely through eating that Esav sold the birthright to Yaakov, 
 and afterwards received the blessing too — 
 for in truth, one who binds himself only to the intellect in every thing 
 and thinks only of the ultimate purpose — the World to Come — 
 has in truth also all the blessings of this world in their fullness — 
 in the aspect of *"for G-d has been gracious to me and I have everything"* [Bereishis 33:11]. And therefore afterwards when Esav said to him: 
 "let us journey and go, and I will go alongside you" [Bereishis 33:12] — 
 implying: be like me — 
 Yaakov replied to him: this is impossible — 
 for the world of this side — the aspect of Esav — 
 and the World to Come — the aspect of Yaakov 
 [which in truth encompasses all the good of this world as well] — 
 are two absolute opposites, like darkness and light — 
 and they cannot coexist together. And therefore: 
 "Let my master please pass before his servant" [Bereishis 33:14] — etc. — 
 for first comes darkness and then light — 
 and yet in truth even the darkness is for the benefit of the light — 
 for the advantage of the light is only evident from within the darkness.
 

 
 [§4]
 And therefore during the meal — even though one is obligated to speak words of Torah — 
 at the very moment of actual eating it is forbidden to speak 
 even words of Torah — 
 lest the windpipe precede the gullet — 
 for the mouth of the windpipe may open 
 and some food may enter it and bring danger — 
 for it is impossible for them to function together simultaneously — 
 for "Esav is a man who knows hunting, a man of the field" [Bereishis 25:27] — 
 and "Yaakov is a wholesome man dwelling in tents" — in the tent of Torah. And therefore during actual eating one must be silent — 
 directing one's thought in great holiness for the sake of Heaven. But since, for the sanctity of thought — which is the aspect of Chochmah — 
 one must give strength to holy Malchus to overpower [the sitra achra], 
 especially during eating and the meal — when one is drawing out clarifications — 
 one must engage in words of Torah — but not during actual eating.
 

 
 [§5]
 Yaakov Avinu did not die — 
 for since the attribute of Yaakov is to look only at the wisdom and life-force in every thing — 
 and even all physical things, like eating, he performs only with this intention — 
 certainly the sitra d'mosa has no hold upon him whatsoever, 
 and he is alive forever.
 

 
 [§6]
 And since the life-force clothed in every food 
 is only from the holy sparks of Chochmah clothed within it — 
 it is forbidden to treat foods with contempt — 
 for Chochmah is in the aspect of honor — 
 as it is said: *"the wise shall inherit honor"* [Mishlei 3:35] — 
 the opposite of the aspect of Esav — of whom it is said "and Esav despised" — as stated.
 

 
 [§7]
 Intermediate waters [between courses] are optional — 
 for this alludes to one who has already merited to bind himself 
 to the holy intellect in every thing — 
 and who has actual attainment in the intellect of each and every thing, 
 each according to its aspect. Certainly this person too must constantly draw upon himself 
 the pure and holy waters — 
 the aspect of the waters of supernal Chochmah and the holy Torah — 
 since he must engage and recognize at every turn a new wisdom — 
 corresponding to each new dish's aspect of holy sparks of Chochmah clothed within it. But since not every mind can bear this, 
 and not every person merits to attain all of this in detail, 
 this washing is only optional — 
 not established as a mitzvah — 
 only the first washing is established, 
 to purify oneself from any impurity and connect oneself 
 in general at least to the holy Torah and Chochmah clothed in every thing.
 

 
 [§8]
 General and specific blessings — 
 and this itself is the matter of why our Sages instituted 
 both general and specific blessings — 
 and within the specific ones there are themselves levels of general and specific — 
 such as borei pri ha'adamah [who creates the fruit of the ground] being general, 
 and borei pri ha'etz [who creates the fruit of the tree] more specific — 
 and wine, due to its importance, has a further specific blessing: borei pri hagafen. And likewise for bread types — 
 borei minei mezonos [who creates species of grain foods] is general, 
 and bread, due to its importance, has the specific blessing HaMotzi — 
 and all of this is understood and explained according to this approach.

aligned_segments.he: כי עושין לו לויה וחיבור עם החיים בכדי שיהיה נקשר באור החים אף לאחר מותו ולא יפול סטרא דמותא ממש ח"ו וע"כ מבטלין ת"ת להוצאת המת.
aligned_segments.en:
For our Sages taught: 
 "Blessed is Hashem day by day" [Tehillim 68:20] — 
 "each day give [thanks for that day's blessings]" — 
 for each act of Hashem is for His sake — 
 and all the variations between one day and the next — 
 certainly each contains a wondrous wisdom 
 of how to draw close to Hashem through it, 
 in a new closeness and new knowledge. And therefore each day one must bless according to [that day's blessings].
 

 
 [§9]
 And wine, due to its great importance — 
 for it gladdens G-d and men, 
 and one recites song only over wine — 
 and our Sages taught: 
 "wine and fragrance make the mind sharp" [Yoma 76b] — 
 and from this the holy life-force clothed within it is most visible and apparent — 
 therefore one must bless it with a specific blessing. And likewise, change of location constitutes an interruption during a meal — 
 for Hashem, as it were, contracts Himself and alludes 
 hints of wisdom to each person through each particular thing 
 according to place and time — 
 as explained in the discourse Meketz Zikaron, Siman 54 — 
 and therefore change of location is also considered a change in this matter. And likewise the matter of things that require an after-blessing 
 specifically in their place [b'mekomam] — due to their importance — 
 and all of this is understood according to the above.

[§7] And one should strive to personally prepare something for Shabbos' needs — for the mitzvah is better performed directly than through an agent — for through every mitzvah holiness is drawn upon the person — in the aspect of "Who sanctified us with His commandments" — and Kodesh is Chochmah — as is known — and therefore one merits through this to bind oneself to holy Chochmah in its fullness through the aspect of the mitzvah — which is the aspect of holy Malchus. And the greater one's effort for the sake of the mitzvah, the greater the reward — and the greater the holiness one merits — for through the effort and strength invested in performing the mitzvah one gives strength to holy Malchus to overpower the kingdom of the sitra achra. And therefore the mitzvah is certainly better performed directly — especially the mitzvah of preparing for Shabbos — which is itself called Kodesh.

סִימָן קע״ז — הִלְכוֹת אוֹנֵס וּמְפַתֶּה

[§1]
The laws of onus and mefateh [rape and seduction]. *"If a man finds a young virgin"* [Shemos 22:15] — etc. — "and he seizes her and lies with her" — "the man who lay with her shall give her father fifty silver pieces" — etc. For since he lay with her and violated her by force — therefore: in addition to having to pay for shame and damage and pain — he must give a fine of fifty silver pieces. Corresponding to what he damaged in her holiness — whose root is from the aspect of Malchus — the aspect of nun. Therefore he must give fifty silver pieces to her father — who is the aspect of Chochmah — the aspect of: "father in wisdom." For there is the root of her source — the aspect of: "father founded the daughter" — the aspect of: "Hashem founded the earth with wisdom." Therefore one must give fifty silver pieces — corresponding to the aspect of nun mentioned — whose number is fifty. And this: "and she shall be his wife" — for since he desired her and came upon her against her will — he is therefore compelled to marry her — and cannot send her away all his days. For since the beginning of their union was only from his side — and by force — therefore he cannot sever the connection and send her away all his days. And see in the holy Zohar — where it is elaborated: that the fifty silver pieces are the foundation of the fifty letters of Shema Yisrael and Baruch Shem — in which is the essential acceptance of Heavenly Kingship. And regarding a seduced woman — where the matter was done with her consent — therefore one must quickly betroth her as a wife — giving her a mohar and kesubah — as is customary for all virgins — so that the union be complete — and that she not be easy in his eyes to send away — as stated in the laws of kesubos.

aligned_segments.he: כי אע"פ שע"י לתמוד תורה נותנים כח למלכות דקדושה ומכניעין סטרא דמותא אעפ"כ לא המדרש עיקר אלא המעשה.
aligned_segments.en:
And then he is exempt from the fine — since he married her as a wife.

[§2]
And if her father absolutely refuses to give her to him — and since she is still under her father's authority — and her father does not agree to give her — therefore he shall weigh money equivalent to the mohar of virgins — and must give a fine of fifty silver pieces — corresponding to nun mentioned — that he damaged in her — as stated.

[§8] And therefore one should sharpen the knife on Erev Shabbos in honor of Shabbos — and this is derived from: *"and they shall prepare [v'heichinu] what they bring"* [Shemos 16:5] — אֵת alludes to the aspect of Malchus — and sikkin [knife] also alludes to the aspects of Malchus and Binah — see the Maurai Or.

סִימָן קע״ח

[§1]
Not to wear the garments of non-Jews. For garments are in the aspect of Malchus — and flow at their root from supernal Chochmah — as has been explained many times. And see in the tale of the children who were exchanged — regarding the garment that the sun makes for the moon — which is the aspect of the newness of the moon [chidushai d'sihara] — and from this aspect is the root of the garments of Israel who are bound to this aspect. But the garments of non-Jews and all their customs flow from the aspect of sun and moon of the sitra achra. And therefore: it is forbidden to walk in their statutes.

סִימָן קע״ח — הִלְכוֹת סוֹטָה

[§1]
The laws of Sotah [the suspected woman]. For since the woman — whose root is from the aspect of Malchus — the last attribute — as it were — which is adjacent to the external — the aspect of: "this Jerusalem — she placed her impurity in her midst" [Eichah 1:9] — etc. — and as explained elsewhere — therefore there is the essential hold of the sitra d'mosa — the aspect of: "her feet descend to death." And therefore she requires great guarding — lest there be any damage to her — G-d forbid. And this is the aspect of: sometimes one must warn her before witnesses — and say to her: do not be secluded with such-and-such a man. "Do not be secluded" specifically — for the way of the yetzer hara is to lurk in secret places — as stated. But he warns her openly and specifically — before witnesses — and with the power of the commandment of holy Torah — of which it is said: "the testimony of Hashem is faithful — it makes wise the simple" — as stated. But even when he warns her in private — she must also be careful to fulfil his words. And therefore: he must not say to her even in private — in such language as to cause her to be forbidden to him — but he rebukes her in private — gently and righteously — with purity and warning — in order to remove the stumbling block and guide her in the straight path. As this language is elaborated in the Shulchan Aruch, this Siman, at its end. And these words allude to the matter elaborated in the discourse Ashrei mentioned — regarding the drawing of these rectifications through Torah study — which is the essential straight path — the aspect of: "for the paths of Hashem are straight" — where it is explained: through Torah — the righteous walk in them — for they receive strength through it. And the wicked stumble in them — for the yetzer hara falls and is nullified through it — until one merits the aspect of: "the words of the wise are heard in gentleness" — see there. For our Sages taught: the yetzer hara — a child and a woman — push away with the left and draw close with the right.

aligned_segments.he: וע"כ מבטלין ת"ת לקיים מצוות הלויית המת במעשה, כי עי"ז מגרשין ומכניעין בחי' סטרא דמותא במעשה ממש וממשיכים בחי' אור החיים.
aligned_segments.en:
And therefore: the matter of warning the woman — and likewise the matter of subduing the yetzer hara — are parallel to each other in many respects — and one learns from the other. For regarding the warning of the woman — there is a dispute in the Gemara: whether it is forbidden to warn her — or permitted. And likewise: whether it is obligatory or voluntary. And likewise: "and if the spirit of jealousy passes over him" — one said: a spirit of impurity — and one said: a spirit of purity (see Sotah 2b and 3a). And likewise in the matter of the yetzer hara — our Sages taught: "let a person always arouse the yetzer tov against the yetzer hara." And this is like the aspect of warning the woman. But there is great weighing in this. For it is already explained: that the yetzer hara lurks in hiding — and sometimes dresses itself in mitzvos. And therefore: sometimes the jealousy itself comes from the side of the yetzer hara — and its intention is to corrupt through this the peace of the home — and create hatred and division of hearts between them — until it causes quarrel — and through this — G-d forbid — even greater corruptions. And therefore a spirit of jealousy such as this is in the aspect of the spirit of impurity — G-d forbid.

[§2]
And this is what is elaborated here in the Shulchan Aruch, section 21: it is a commandment of the Sages — etc. — to warn their wives. And all who do not hold firm regarding his wife — etc. — behold he is a sinner. And all who warns his wife — the spirit of purity has entered him. And one should not warn her amidst laughter — etc. — and not amidst quarrel — and not to cast fear upon her — etc. And there in section 22: one should not rush to warn — etc. — but rather rebuke her gently. As stated.

aligned_segments.he: וע,F למאן דלא קרי ולא תני מאחר שגם בחייו היה רחוק מאור התורה אשר היא עיקר החיים ע"כ אין מבטלין ת"ת בשבילו.
aligned_segments.en:
And likewise in the matter of the battle with the yetzer hara — there are also these aspects. For sometimes through provoking against it — through this it is subdued and flees before the yetzer tov. But sometimes — specifically through becoming too angered against it — beyond the level of one's mind — through this the yetzer hara overpowers one even more afterwards — until it brings one to what it brings one to. And this is seen palpably many times. And this is the aspect of: "do not be overly righteous" [Koheles 7:16] — and much of this is in the discourse of v'al tarshe'a harbeh. And therefore: every clever person acts with knowledge in these matters. And the essential completion of the rectification in its fullness is only through Torah study — through which one gives strength to holy Malchus — the root of the aspect of the yetzer tov — until it receives life-force from the aspect of Chochmah. And then the yetzer hara — the aspect of foolishness — automatically falls and is nullified entirely — for a little light drives away much darkness — as understood within in the discourse mentioned. And this is hinted in the verse in Koheles 9: "a small city and few men in it" — which speaks of the battle with the yetzer hara — as our Sages taught. And: "a poor wise man was found in it" — the aspect of the yetzer tov. And: "he saved the city through his wisdom" — etc. And it says: "I said — wisdom is better than might." But: "the wisdom of the poor man is despised — and his words are not heard." For the yetzer hara strengthens itself essentially against this very thing — to despise the wisdom of the yetzer tov — and not to hear its words. And it concludes: "the words of the wise are heard in gentleness" — etc.

[§3]
For in truth — according to the strengthening and spreading of the yetzer hara — the words of the yetzer tov would not be heard at all. For everything the yetzer tov says — the yetzer hara overpowers it even more — with its impudence — in great noise and shouting.

aligned_segments.he: אלא מי שצריך להתעסק עמו.
aligned_segments.en:
But through the fact that the words of the yetzer tov are specifically in gentleness and calmly — through this specifically — its words are heard even more — the aspect of: "the words of the wise are heard in gentleness — more than the shouting of a ruler among fools" [Koheles 9:17]. And this alludes to the aspect of the wonders of the rectification of Torah study — which are themselves in the aspect of: "the words of the wise are heard in gentleness." For all their words are in gentleness and calmness and wondrous wisdom. And through this — each time more power is added to holy Malchus — until the moonlight becomes as the sunlight — and one merits grace. And through this all requests and prayers are accepted. The aspect of Tav.

[§4]
And all of this is alluded to in the word b'nachas [in gentleness]: Nun-Ches-Tav — as explained within. And through this specifically — the words of the yetzer tov are heard — and one merits to conquer the battle of the inclination in its fullness. For after all the drawing of these rectifications — one adds yet more in prayers and supplications and entreaties before Hashem — and the Holy One accepts one's prayer and fulfils one's request — to conquer the battle in its fullness. The aspect of what is said of David the King: *"Ask of Me — and I shall give nations as your inheritance — and the ends of the earth as your possession"* [Tehillim 2:8] — etc. And see in the Targum on these verses. And it concluded there on the verse: "the words of the wise" — etc.: milei d'tzlosa d'chachimaya b'chasha miskabalin kadam maru alma — etc. — as stated.

תַּם וְנִשְׁלַם שֶׁבַח לָאֵל בּוֹרֵא עוֹלָם
Completed and finished — praise to G-d, Creator of the world.

ב׳ נ׳ ל׳ כ׳ ו׳ א׳ ע׳ י׳

Nachas HaShulchan — Part VIII (Even HaEzer) · Simanim 1–178 · Complete

Translated faithfully from the Hebrew of Rabbi Nachman of Tchehrin ז״ל

Na Nach Nachma Nachman MayUman ✦

[§1] It is permitted to begin labor on Erev Shabbos near twilight even though the labor completes itself on Shabbos [Siman 252] — for the essential clarifications that are clarified through labor all occur only through the power of Chochmah — which is called reishis [beginning] — as stated. And therefore when the beginning and commencement of the labor — which is performed by the person who possesses wisdom and intellect — takes place before Shabbos — even if it is then completed on Shabbos on its own — there is no concern — since the person does nothing more — it all happens through the power of the beginning made before Shabbos. Except when there is concern he may assist in the labor on Shabbos itself — such as lest he stoke the coals — in that case it is forbidden. And in this is also explained what is stated in Simanim 253, 254, 255, 257, 258, and so on.

סִימָן קע״ט

[§1]
Not to practice sorcery or divination or consulting omens — etc. For we must bind ourselves only to the holy light of the intellect in every thing — as stated.

aligned_segments.he: אבל מי שהיה דבוק באור התורה ע,י שקרא או שנה מבטלין בשבילו עד ששים רבוא שהם בחי' שיעור קומת הקדושה בחי' ששים רבוא אותיות לתורה וששים רבוא נשמות ישראל המושרשים בהם ומקבלים על ידם אור החיים דקדושה.
aligned_segments.en:
Therefore one must walk in wholeness — and not investigate the future — but accept everything with love and in wholeness. And then one will be His and His portion — as Rashi explains on the verse: "you shall be wholehearted with Hashem your G-d" [Devarim 18:13] — as stated. For since the essential goal of our intention is only to draw close to Him — through every thing — how is it possible for us to pursue schemes and investigate futures — and especially through the evil stratagems of sorcery and the like? Rather one must accept everything with love — and bind oneself to Hashem in all that comes upon one — for He alone is our portion and the pleasantness of our lot.

[§2]
And therefore it is truly said of Yaakov — who merited the aspect of holy light of intellect — that "Yaakov was a wholesome man" [Bereishis 25:27] — as cited in the discourse mentioned — on the verse: "Ashrei temimei darech." And therefore also illusion of the eyes is forbidden — for through this one damages the aspect of holy eyes. And this is the aspect of the prohibition of doresh el hameisim [consulting the dead] — for through this one binds oneself to the sitra d'mosa — the opposite of the holy life-force.

[§3]
And this is the aspect of: *"to the living — not to the dead"* [Yeshayahu 8:19]. And this is what is cited in the holy Zohar: "those are the ones who are called living." And therefore it is forbidden to heal oneself through words of Torah — unless for the sake of saving a life. For since one has already been afflicted and the hold of the sitra achra has come upon one — from which is the root of all sicknesses and illnesses — G-d forbid — all of which comes through neglect of Torah — as our Sages taught: he should ascribe it to neglect of Torah. Therefore how can one receive healing through the special quality of reciting words of Torah alone — saying them over the wound? Rather: one must first repent fully for one's deeds — and truly accept the yoke of Torah — and then one will automatically receive healing — as it is written: *"and he shall repent and be healed"* [Yeshayahu 6:10] — and it is written: *"healing shall be to your flesh"* [Mishlei 3:8] — etc. — and as our Sages taught. But to protect oneself from harmful spirits — so that they not harm one — it is permitted to recite verses. For certainly through words of Torah the sitra achra is driven away — as our Sages taught: all who engage in Torah — harmful spirits flee from them. And this: *"all the nations"* [Devarim 18:14] — *"hearken to soothsayers and diviners — but as for you — not so has Hashem your G-d given you"* — *"a prophet"* — etc. — *"like me He will raise up for you"* — *"and I will place My words in his mouth"* — etc. [ibid. 15, 18]. For the Holy One informs Israel of the future through His holy prophets — who draw their power from the aspect of Moshe our teacher — whose root is in supernal Chochmah — the aspect of: "face of Moshe is as the face of the sun" — the aspect of: "a prophet has a wise heart" — as our Sages expounded.

[§2] They would sound the shofar on Erev Shabbos to separate the people from labor [Siman 256] — for the blasts of the shofar are the aspect of the arousal of the mochin from their slumber — as is known. For the wisdom and mochin of the weekdays are the aspect of mochin d'katnus [small consciousness] — the aspect of sleep — compared to the mochin one merits to receive on holy Shabbos.

aligned_segments.he: וע,כ מבטלין ת"ת גם להכנסת כלה.
aligned_segments.en:
And therefore on the weekdays they are days of labor — and therefore one sounds [the shofar] on Erev Shabbos to separate the people from labor and prepare them to receive the holiness of the Chochmah and mochin that shine on Shabbos. And this too is the aspect of the blasts themselves — as our Sages taught: "the sounding of the shofar is wisdom and not labor."

סִימָן ק״פ

[§1]
And therefore: it is forbidden to incise a tattoo or to make a bald patch for the dead or for idolatry. For these are from the customs of non-Jews — who are bound to the sitra d'mosa — the aspect of: "they shall die without wisdom" — and therefore they mark their bodies as a remembrance of the dead or of idolatry. But Israel — who are bound to the living G-d — until even in their death they are called living. Therefore all of this is forbidden to them. And this: "you are children" — etc. — "you shall not cut yourselves" — etc. — for the departure of one of Israel — G-d forbid — is only like a king who sends for his son to return to his father's house in peace — to delight with him — etc. — and as our Sages expounded this.

[§3] The mitzvah of bathing in hot water on Erev Shabbos [Siman 260] — and it is explained in the kavanos that this is the secret of the flame of fire that descends on Erev Shabbos to subdue the klippos — meaning one draws the illumination of supernal Chochmah — the aspect of Yaakov and Yosef — who are the aspect of the flame of fire — as stated — as it is written: *"and the house of Yaakov shall be fire and the house of Yosef a flame"* [Ovadyah 1:18] — and through this one burns and subdues the klippos — the aspect of Esav — the kingdom of the sitra achra — the aspect of the yetzer hara's fire — for from fire they came and fire will consume them. And this is the aspect of: "always let a person arouse the good inclination against the evil inclination" — and the arousal is from the aspect of judgments and gevuros — the aspect of fire. And afterwards one immerses in the mikveh — which is the aspect of encompassing oneself in the waters of supernal chesed — which flow from the aspect of the holy supernal intellect — the aspect of chesed and mercy.

סִימָן קפ״א — דִּין מַיִם אַחֲרוֹנִים

 

 
 [§1]
 For all the time that Hashem, as it were, desires the continued existence of the sitra achra — 
 for the sake of [preserving] the power of free choice — 
 one must therefore draw for it also some spark of holy life-force — 
 but only enough for its sustenance and in great contraction — 
 and through this specifically one subdues it — 
 as is understood in the discourse Marikim Sakeihem, Siman 17 — 
 and this is elaborated much in the holy Zohar. And this is the matter of the mayim acharonim [final waters] taken after the meal — 
 for since eating is a physical, animalistic matter — 
 it being one of the things in which man resembles an animal — as our Sages taught — 
 and in particular since the implements of eating are from the side of Esav — as stated — 
 it is impossible for some degree of foolishness not to gain hold through this. Therefore one gives them their portion through the final waters — 
 so that they not grow stronger, G-d forbid.
 

 
 [§2]
 And our Sages taught that one takes final waters 
 on account of Melach Sedomis [Sodomite salt], which blinds the eyes — 
 and a trace [of it] is mixed among the pure salt, 
 for in the holy salt [of the Ketores] there is hidden also a trace of this. And in the intentions of the Ketores it is explained that Melach Sedomis 
 is the secret of Tidal king of nations [Bereishis 14:1] — 
 and the Midrash explains that Tidal king of nations alludes to the kingdom of Edom — etc. — 
 and it is known that the exile of Edom encompasses both Esav and Yishmael, 
 who are the clouds that blind the eyes — 
 and therefore Melach Sedomis blinds the eyes — 
 which are the aspect of Chochmah — as it is written: 
 *"and the eyes of them both were opened"* [Bereishis 3:7] — 
 and Rashi explains: this was said regarding wisdom.
 

 
 [§3]
 And it has already been explained above that Chochmah is in the aspect of salt — 
 and therefore there is found among a kor of salt one kernel of Sodomite salt — 
 so that they too should have some nourishment from it in great contraction. And in order that they not grow stronger and blind the eyes — 
 meaning confuse a person from looking with open eyes 
 at the holy wisdom and intellect in every thing — 
 one must take the final waters — as stated. And this is what is explained in the kavanos and cited in the Siddur Kol Yaakov: 
 that the final waters serve to drive away the sitra achra from the table 
 and give them their portion — etc. — 
 and this is what our Sages taught: 
 on account of Melach Sedomis which blinds the eyes — 
 which is the secret of the strong klippa — etc. — 
 which is the secret of the shakyan — the old and foolish king — etc. — 
 see there — and it corresponds to our matter — 
 for the kingdom of the sitra achra — the aspect of the yetzer hara — 
 is the Satan — the aspect of Esav — the aspect of the old and foolish king — 
 for "the fool desires not understanding" [Mishlei 18:2] — as explained within.

aligned_segments.he: כי המשכת התיקונים הנ" להם בחי' יחוד חתן וכלה.
aligned_segments.en:
And therefore: 
 melech zakein u'ksil [old and foolish king] together with the word count 
 in numerical value equals Esav.

סִימָן קפ״א

[§1]
The prohibition of shaving the pe'os of the head and the beard. See in the kavanos. For the hairs of the head are from the aspect of gevuros and judgments. And therefore one must shave them — for from the aspect of overly strengthened judgments — the sitra achra — the aspect of Esav the hairy man — suckles from there. Only one must leave the pe'os — which allude to the aspect of Malchus. For the building of Malchus — through which one merits to receive from the light of Chochmah — is from the aspect of gevuros — as is known. This is the aspect of dina d'malchusa [the law of the kingdom]. And therefore it is forbidden to shave the pe'os. And the hairs of the beard are in the aspect of kindness and mercy — whose root is from the aspect of Chochmah — the aspect of: "a sage — this one acquired wisdom" — the aspect of: "the splendor of the face" — the aspect of: "a man's wisdom illuminates his face." And therefore it is forbidden to shave them. And also: the hairs of the beard allude to the thirteen attributes through which the Torah is expounded — the aspect of Torah study mentioned. And likewise they allude to the thirteen attributes of mercy — which are the root of all prayer. And therefore one does not appoint a prayer leader unless his beard has filled out — as explained in the Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chaim, Siman 53. It emerges: in the pe'os and the beard — all these rectifications are alluded to — which are the aspect of the general totality of Israel's holiness — as stated.

[§4] Three things one must say at twilight on Erev Shabbos [Siman 260 cont.]: "Did you tithe?" — corresponding to the aspect of Malchus — the aspect of maaser [tithe] — "Did you make the eruv?" — corresponding to Torah study — as explained in the Tikkunnim: eruv is the middle pillar — the aspect of Torah — as is known — "Light the lamp" — corresponding to the illumination of supernal intellect that shines even in the dark — in the aspect of: *"for You light my lamp, Hashem — my G-d illuminates my darkness"* [Tehillim 18:29].

סִימָן קפ״ב — בִּרְכַּת הַמָּזוֹן

 

 
 [§1]
 See in the kavanos where it is explained that 
 the secret of the four blessings of Birchas HaMazon 
 is the drawing of the mochin to the Nukva [feminine aspect] — 
 meaning, as stated above: 
 that the illumination of the holy Chochmah — 
 which is the totality of the mochin — 
 should shine upon holy Malchus — 
 until she is in the aspect of: 
 *"the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun"* [Yeshayahu 30:26] — 
 as is explained within.
 

 
 [§2]
 And this is what our Sages said: 
 the first blessing was established by Moshe — who is the aspect of the sun. The second [Birkas HaAretz] was established by Yehoshua — 
 who is the aspect of the moon.

aligned_segments.he: כי המשכת התיקונים הנ"ל הם בחי' יחוד חתן וכלה בשרשם כידוע.
aligned_segments.en:
And this is the blessing of the Land — 
 for the Land of Israel is also in this aspect — 
 and therefore it was Yehoshua specifically who brought Israel into the Land — 
 as is explained in the Zohar. And therefore one must mention there also Bris [covenant] and Torah — 
 for its essential power is through the holy Torah — 
 through which one subdues the kingdom of the sitra achra — 
 the aspect of Esav and Yishmael — 
 and this is the aspect of Bris — 
 the aspect of milah [circumcision] and priah [uncovering] — 
 and it is also simply known that through the mitzvah of circumcision 
 one weakens the power of the yetzer hara — 
 and the entire Torah depends upon the Bris — as is known.
 

 
 [§3]
 The third blessing — on the building of Yerushalayim 
 and the Holy Temple and the Davidic Kingdom — 
 was established by Dovid and Shlomo — 
 for Yerushalayim encompasses all of the above — 
 for it had great sages — in the aspect of "Rabbas bagoyim" [Eichah 1:1] — 
 and our Sages expounded: "great in intellect." 
 And it was the royal city — 
 and essentially the revelation of His Kingship is in Yerushalayim — 
 as it is said: *"Hashem shall reign forever — your G-d O Zion"* [Tehillim 146:10]. And in it was the primary study of Torah — 
 as it is said: "arise and go up" — and it is written: 
 *"for from Zion shall the Torah go forth"* [Yeshayahu 2:3]. And in it is the primary chen [grace] — overall beauty — etc. — 
 and there is the primary place of prayer. The Beis HaMikdash itself certainly encompasses all of the above in the utmost perfection. And likewise the kingdom of Dovid and Shlomo encompasses all the above — 
 for in the days of Shlomo "the moon was at its fullness" [Zohar] — 
 and they merited wondrous wisdom and Torah and chen and prayer.
 

 
 [§4]
 The fourth blessing was established for the slain of Beitar — 
 who were given burial — 
 for then they saw that even in our service He has not abandoned us — etc. — 
 for even though the kingdom of the sitra achra overpowered 
 and thousands and myriads of Israel were slain — 
 and moreover they were not permitted to be buried — 
 yet Hashem performed a great miracle that they did not decompose — 
 for it is impossible for the flesh of a dead person not to decompose — 
 and afterwards they were also given burial — 
 in the aspect of *"and the dust shall return to the earth as it was"* [Koheles 12:7]. For the bodies of holy Israel are in their root 
 the aspect of the contractions through which one merits to receive fully 
 the light of the intellect and life-force — 
 the aspect of the soul. And therefore after one's passing the body is buried in the earth — 
 whose root is the aspect of Malchus — the aspect of contraction — 
 and the spirit returns to G-d — etc. — 
 in the aspect of *"but the soul of my master shall be bound in the bundle of life"* [Shemuel I 25:29]. And therefore this was established as the fourth blessing — 
 HaTov v'HaMeitiv [Who is good and does good] — 
 as stated in the laws governing meal conduct.
 

 
 [§5]
 A mitzvah to recite Birchas HaMazon over a cup [of wine] — 
 for the cup is the aspect of Malchus — as is known — 
 and one holds it in one's hand with five fingers 
 corresponding to the Five Books of Torah — 
 which are the essential power and strengthening of Malchus — 
 and the wine within it is the aspect of daas [knowledge] and Chochmah — as stated. And therefore it must be whole — 
 for holy Chochmah and Malchus are in the aspect of completeness — as stated.
 

 
 [§6]
 The cup requires rinsing on the inside and wiping on the outside — 
 meaning its inside should match its outside — 
 see Tikkunnei Zohar, Tikkun 28 — 
 in the aspect of: "as my heart is, so I said to his brothers" [Bereishis 44:20] — 
 and the verse: *"my mouth shall speak wisdom and the meditation of my heart shall be understanding"* [Tehillim 49:4] — 
 and likewise: *"the heart of the wise guides his mouth"* [Mishlei 16:23] — 
 the aspect of Malchus — the mouth — 
 the opposite of the kingdom of the sitra achra — the yetzer hara — 
 the aspect of Esav — who is impure and reprehensible 
 both inside and outside — 
 and even if he sometimes speaks something correct with his mouth, 
 "seven abominations are in his heart" [Mishlei 26:25] — 
 in the aspect of: *"for he hunted with his mouth"* — said of Esav — 
 which is the aspect of what is explained within 
 regarding the yetzer hara clothing himself at times in mitzvos.

סִימָן קפ״ב

[§1]
"A man shall not wear a woman's garment" — etc. — for man and woman are rooted in the aspects of sun and moon — intellect and Malchus — and from there is the root of their garments — as stated. And therefore each must guard its own aspect — and not exchange or replace — and leave one's boundary — G-d forbid. For through this the sitra achra suckles — G-d forbid — the aspect of the union of the sitra achra — the aspect of adultery — G-d forbid. And see in Likutay Halachos Yoreh Deah on this matter — and in Choshen Mishpat, the Laws of Deposits — on this discourse — and you will understand further.

[§5] The Shabbos lamps [Siman 261] — and it is explained in the kavanos that they correspond to Binah and Malchus — meaning Malchus then receives the illumination of supernal Chochmah through Binah — for they are the two companions that never separate — as is known. And this is the aspect of: "One who wishes to become wise should face south — for the Menorah is in the south" — as our Sages taught.

aligned_segments.he: וע,כ גם מצוות הכנסת כלה במעשה ממש הוא גדול מאד עד שמבטלין ת"ת בשבילה.
aligned_segments.en:
And this is the aspect of the setting of the table on Shabbos — for Malchus ascends then from the aspect of poverty to the aspect of wealth — in the aspect of the royal table — in the aspect of: "one who wishes to become wealthy should face north — for the Table is in the north."

סִימָן קפ״ג וְכוּ׳ — הִלְכוֹת נִדָּה

[§1]
The laws of niddah. See Zohar Pinchas 226b: "the children of niddah — etc. — the Heh departed from its place — which is the Matron — the yetzer tov — and in its place entered a maidservant — the yetzer hara — and the secret of the matter: as a plague appeared to me in the house — and this is the impure blood of the niddah" — etc. It is explained: the impurity of niddah is from the aspect of the yetzer hara — the aspect of the kingdom of the sitra achra — the aspect of the maidservant: "when a maidservant supplants her mistress." And this is the aspect of what is cited: that Esav suckled from the impure blood of niddah in Rivkah's womb — and therefore he was red and a man of blood. And therefore: the impurity of niddah is in the aspect of nega — as stated — for nega is the aspect of the opposite of oneg — which is the aspect of holy Chochmah — as is known. And therefore: children of niddah are afflicted with tzara'as — as our Sages taught.

[§2]
And since the essential hold of the yetzer hara is in the seven attributes — the aspect of: "for seven times a righteous man falls and rises" — as is known — for in the aspect of the mochin — which are above the attributes — it has no hold at all. For a person does not transgress unless the mochin have departed from him and madness and a spirit of folly have entered him. And therefore: she shall be in her niddah state for seven days. And by Torah law there are many distinctions between a niddah and a zavah — and all is explained according to the above — but this is not the place to elaborate. And already our Sages taught: the daughters of Israel were stringent upon themselves — that even if they see only a drop of blood the size of a mustard seed — they sit seven clean days upon it. For such is the way of the yetzer hara: today it says to him: do such — etc. — and at first it resembles a thread of a spider's web — and then — etc. — as our Sages taught. And therefore one must guard against it and purify oneself from its impurity — even in the smallest amount.

[§3]
And this is the aspect of the seven clean days — to purify all the attributes — which are the aspect of the seven days — so that there be no hold of evil in them whatsoever. And in particular one who has already stumbled in the hold of the yetzer hara — even in the smallest amount — must be even more precise regarding oneself — and greatly regret — and repent over the past — and guard oneself greatly for the future — not to give any room to the hold of the inclination in any of one's attributes — even in the smallest amount — but all of them shall be clean and pure.

[§4]
And afterwards she immerses in pure water containing forty se'ah — so that her entire body ascends in them. Meaning: one nullifies all the physicality of one's body — only for the aspect of the waters of holy Torah — which are the aspect of forty se'ah — for each se'ah is six kav — and likewise each kav is four revi'is — which is the aspect of the forty days of the giving of the Torah — and each day is twenty-four hours — which is the aspect of the forty se'ah mentioned. And also: the waters are the aspect of the waters of holy daas — the aspect of supernal intellect — through which one completes one's purification.

aligned_segments.he: כי זה עיקר תכלית לימוד התורה להכניע עי"ז בחי' היצה"ר שהוא סיטרא דמותא שזה בחי' הוצאת המת וליתן כח למלכות דקדושה שהיא בחי' הכלה הקדושה כידוע.
aligned_segments.en:
For holy Torah and holy intellect illuminate one in all one's ways — until one merits to draw close to Hashem through every thing in the world — even through physical matters — the aspect of: waters in which one's entire body ascends — as stated.

[§5]
And this is the aspect of the fixing of the woman's veses [menstrual cycle]. For there are times — and there are times for good and times for bad — G-d forbid. And all is according to the aspect of the ascent and descent of Malchus — G-d forbid — the aspect of the days of the moon's filling and its deficiency — the aspect of the building of holy Malchus and its destruction — G-d forbid — as is elaborated on this in our Sages' teachings. And these times pass upon every person according to one's aspect — in those times that one knows within oneself — that one is accustomed to be provoked by one's inclination more — which is the aspect of times of evil. And the essential is at the beginning of these times. And therefore our Sages taught: the standard veses of an intermediate cycle is once every thirty days — which are the general days of the moon's filling and deficiency — as stated. And there are also vestos of the body — such as through excessive eating — and the like. And likewise spiritually: there are those who know within themselves that sometimes when they stumble in some excessive eating and drinking — or the like — in some physical matter — then their inclination is provoked upon them more. Especially when one knows one has already stumbled many times — G-d forbid — through such things. Therefore in addition to needing to guard oneself greatly from this — even when one has already stumbled — G-d forbid — again in such a physical matter — even if it is a matter of permission and is allowed — even so one must immediately afterwards check and be extra careful — and search within oneself — whether through this the hold of the yetzer hara has seized — which is the aspect of the impurity of niddah — as stated. And according to this approach it is easy for the discerning to explain many more laws and rulings in this matter.

[§6] And therefore it is a mitzvah to honor Shabbos in fine garments — for it has already been explained that the supernal intellects are the aspect of the garments of honor of the person — and therefore it is a mitzvah to wear white garments then — corresponding to the supernal whiteness — in the aspect of *"and streams from Lebanon"* — from the whiteness of the brain [levunah d'mocha]. And לָבָן contains the letters ל-ב-ן — which are the initials of: lamed-beis nativot — the thirty-two paths of Chochmah — and also ל״ב נוּ״ן — lamed-beis and nun — meaning one binds the nun — the aspect of Malchus — to the 32 paths of Chochmah.

סִימָן קצ״ב — בִּרְכַּת זִימּוּן

 

 
 [§1]
 And therefore when three [men] are present, they recite Zimun — 
 and the senior recites and two respond after him — etc. — 
 for three of Israel encompass the three aspects mentioned above — 
 namely: Chochmah, Malchus, and Torah — 
 and each one of them is comprised of three. For Chochmah encompasses Chochmah, Binah, and Daas [knowledge]. And Torah is threefold — as our Sages taught [it was given to a three-fold nation, etc.].

aligned_segments.he: ולייחדה עם דודה שהוא בחי' חמה בחי' חתן בחי' והוא כחתן יוצא מחופתו כנ"ל וזה בחי' מבטלין תלמוד תורה להוצאת המת ולהכנסת כלה.
aligned_segments.en:
And Malchus is the aspect of: 
 "Hashem reigns — Hashem has reigned — Hashem shall reign." 
 And this is the aspect of why in the fourth blessing — HaTov v'HaMeitiv — 
 one must say three mentions of kingship, three goodnesses, and three acts of kindness. And therefore when three recite Zimun — 
 one recites and two listen and respond — 
 this is the aspect of "the words of the wise heard in quietness" — as explained within.
 

 
 [§2]
 And therefore one begins: "Hav lan v'nevoreich" [Give us and let us bless] — 
 and it is cited in the Siddur Kol Yaakov that haben lan 
 contains the letters of Levanah [moon] — 
 for this is the aspect of the filling of the moon — as stated — 
 and this is what one says: "b'reshus" [with the permission of] — etc. — 
 "let us bless." 
 And they respond: "Blessed is He from Whose bounty we have eaten, 
 and through Whose goodness we live" — 
 for the essential life-force is only through the good — 
 which is the Torah and the Chochmah and the holy intellect clothed in every thing — as stated.
 

 
 [§3]
 And when ten are present — 
 "among ten the Shechinah is present" — 
 therefore one invites with [G-d's] Name — 
 for there is there a greater revelation of G-dliness. And therefore one must try to obtain a cup of blessing to recite over — 
 as explained in Shulchan Aruch at the end of Siman 201 — 
 and it is cited in the Zohar that through this one merits longevity — 
 for through this one reveals and draws the light of holy Chochmah and intellect — 
 which is the source of life — as stated.

[§7] And therefore one is strict about the Shabbos lamps — that the oil and wicks should be valid — so that the oil flows after the wick — for the wick alludes to Malchus and the oil to Chochmah — as is known — and therefore they must be joined and unified in a complete union — that no aspect of the kingdom of the sitra achra of Chochmah and Malchus should have any hold — G-d forbid — so that the holy light burns well and does not go out — and so that one not come to desecrate Shabbos.

סִימָן ר״א

[§1]
The laws of mikvaos. See there the many distinctions in law between a spring and a mikveh of rainwater — and the like — and all is somewhat understood according to the above. For a spring is from the aspect of supernal Chochmah — as is known. And therefore it purifies even when the water is flowing. For it is in the aspect of: "a flowing spring — the source of wisdom" — from which the light goes and spreads to all levels — the aspect of: "let your springs spread outward" [Mishlei 5:16]. And therefore one can draw close to Hashem through every thing in the world — through the intellect that illuminates a person. For it is in the aspect of: "going and shining until the day is established" — the aspect of flowing water — that the waters go and flow even far from the place of their springing. But the mikveh is in the aspect of Malchus — which has nothing of its own — only what is influenced upon it from aspects and levels of holiness above its own — the aspect of rainwater and the like — that gather and are collected into the mikveh. And it is only in the aspect of measure and contraction — to receive the light and life-force through it. And therefore it purifies only through ashboron [still water] — that the water within it be gathered and collected — for it is from this aspect.

[§2]
(See Maurai Or.) And there is yet much to explain in this — and it is somewhat self-evident to the one who studies it.

[§1] And this is what [the Sages] said: one who is traveling and Shabbos overtakes him on the road — he may not place his purse upon his donkey — for he is commanded regarding [the donkey's] resting — but should give his purse to a non-Jew — etc. For even a donkey — which is an impure animal and is from the aspect of the sitra achra — nonetheless, since it belongs to a Jew, it has already gained some hold in the side of holiness — for it has become a chariot toward it — and therefore one is commanded regarding its resting. And therefore he gives his purse to the non-Jew who has no part in holiness.

aligned_segments.he: היינו כנ"ל:
aligned_segments.en:
And moreover — this was only permitted regarding money that already belongs to him — for the money of a Jew too has a root in holiness — as is stated elsewhere: *"in the shadow of wisdom, in the shadow of silver"* [Koheles 7:12] — and likewise holy wealth is from the aspect of holy Malchus — as stated above. But money that has not yet come into the Jew's hands — such as if he found a lost object — he may not give it even to the non-Jew — for it is forbidden to damage the holiness of Shabbos even through a non-Jew — as stated. And therefore if there is no non-Jew with him — he is permitted to place [the purse] upon the donkey — but only in the manner described in the Shulchan Aruch — see there — and from this the other matters explained in this Siman are understood.

סִימָן ר״ב — בִּרְכַּת הַפֵּרוֹת

 
 [§1]
 It has already been explained regarding what our Sages instituted — 
 general and specific blessings — 
 and every thing in which the light of the holy intellect shines more vividly — 
 and through which one merits to draw close to Hashem more — 
 they instituted a blessing of its own because of its importance — 
 such as bread and wine — etc. — as stated. And from this many particulars in these laws are self-evident.

[§2]
 Precedence in blessings goes to what is most beloved [Siman 211] — 
 for whatever is customarily most beloved to a person — 
 presumably the spiritual life-force most suited and close to his soul 
 is clothed within it — 
 and therefore it takes precedence in blessing. And likewise what belongs to the Seven Species 
 with which the Land of Israel is praised — 
 which is the aspect of holy Malchus — 
 and its air makes one wise — 
 presumably within these species is clothed 
 the light of Chochmah and holy life-force most vividly. And of these species themselves — 
 whatever is mentioned closest to the word eretz [land] in the verse — 
 presumably the holiness of the Land shines within it more — 
 and therefore it takes precedence in blessing.

[§3]
 And therefore one blesses over the essential item and exempts the secondary — 
 for since that is the essential thing — 
 one must bind the essential to the holy intellect and life-force clothed within it — 
 and the secondary is automatically included within it. And some say that if the secondary is more beloved, 
 one blesses over it first — 
 due to the merit of what is beloved — as stated.
 

 
 [§4]
 And since the essential blessing is to bind oneself 
 to the life-force and Chochmah in every thing — 
 and this is impossible except through the aspect of Malchus — 
 our Sages therefore taught, and it is explained in Siman 214: 
 any blessing that does not contain mention of [G-d's] Name and Kingship is not a blessing — 
 for the essential wisdom and knowledge is only the knowledge of His Name — 
 and in the Zohar they said: 
 "What is His Name? This is Chochmah." 
 And therefore the blessing must contain mention of Name and Kingship.

[§5]
 Responding Amen after a blessing [Siman 215] — 
 for Amen in numerical value equals [the Names] Havayah and Adnus — 
 which is the aspect of uniting Malchus with her Beloved — 
 the moon receiving light from the sun — 
 which is the aspect of Chochmah. And therefore our Sages taught: 
 "Whoever responds Amen with all his power and intention" — 
 which is also from the aspect of Chochmah and his life-force — 
 "the gates of Gan Eden are opened for him" — 
 which are the aspects of lower Chochmah and upper Chochmah — 
 meaning he himself also merits to enter the gates of holy Chochmah 
 through the aspect of Malchus — 
 which is the aspect of lower Chochmah — as is known — 
 and therefore he merits to respond Amen even in the World to Come.
 

 
 
 
 סִימָן רט״ז–רי״ז — בִּרְכַּת הָרֵיחַ וְהַבְּשָׂמִים

[§1]
 For fragrance does not enter the body — 
 it only rises to the brain — 
 where the dwelling of the light of the intellect and the soul is — 
 and the spices themselves are the aspect of Malchus — as is known. And therefore one must bless over fragrance as well — 
 and bind oneself to the holy life-force and intellect clothed within it — 
 and draw close to Hashem through it. Only since it does not enter and remain within the body — 
 rather its pleasure passes and departs immediately — 
 for in its root it is a spiritual and very refined matter — 
 therefore one does not recite a blessing after it.

[§2]
 And this is the aspect of 
 *"and he smelled the scent of his garments and blessed him"* [Bereishis 27:27] — 
 said concerning Yaakov — 
 and our Sages taught that the scent of Gan Eden entered with him — 
 which is the aspects of lower and upper Chochmah mentioned above — 
 which are the source of blessing — as stated — 
 therefore "and he blessed him."
 

 
 [§3]
 And therefore there are also general and specific blessings over fragrances — 
 all as stated above. And therefore it was customary to bless over incense and fragrance after the meal — 
 to show that the side of Yaakov has prevailed 
 and Esav — the yetzer hara — has no hold in the meal — 
 for the meal was intended only for the life of the soul — 
 which is the fragrance — as our Sages taught. And this is the aspect of: *"the righteous eats to satisfy his soul"* [Mishlei 13:25]. And therefore one does not bless over a fragrance that has no substance — 
 for it is impossible to receive the light of the intellect 
 except through the aspect of Malchus — 
 the aspect of contraction — 
 from which is the root of all things from which a person receives his life-force.
